title: local-ci-prober: add fast preflight hermetic runner and dependency provenance stamp
author: Marina Alvarez
description: Context: Developer feedback and oncall incidents showed we needed a lighter, hermetic presubmit that developers can run locally to reproduce CI release smoke quickly without full integration tests. This PR adds a small, platform-agnostic binary (local-ci-prober) plus CI bindings and a deterministic dependency provenance stamp to make local preflight runs fast, reproducible, and auditable. Motivation: reduce iteration time for infra and runtime changes, catch release-hook regressions early, and attach a build provenance token to artifacts for later debugging and rollbacks. What this changes: introduces tools/local-ci-prober (Go) — a minimal runtime that reads our existing build-manifest v2, executes a subset of pipeline stages in-process (lint, unit-test-shim, quick-compile-check, smoke-runner) with deterministic toolchain snapshots; adds scripts/provenance-stamp.go which computes a compact, reproducible manifest-hash+env fingerprint and writes provenance.json into build artifacts; adds .github/workflows/presubmit-fastpath.yaml which integrates the local prober as an optional fast-check in the hosted CI; updates docs/dev/local-preflight.md with usage, failure triage, and recommended local cache warmups; updates Makefile targets for make preflight-local and make stamp-provenance; wire-up in release automation to emit provenance token to release metadata when the full pipeline runs. Safety and opt-in: local-ci-prober defaults to non-destructive checks and has an --offline flag to run entirely without network. It is opt-in for maintainers but recommended in CONTRIBUTING.md. Tests and validation: unit tests for the prober harness and integration smoke tests that validate stamp reproducibility across two toolchain image variants. We also added CI gating in presubmit-fastpath to run the prober in the runner pool and allow fastfeedback on trivial infra-only changes. Rollout: staged rollout — feature flag ci.fast_preflight.enabled=false by default; enable for core infra teams during evaluation. Related tickets: ENG-2345 (local preflight), ENG-2401 (provenance for release artifacts), SUP-421 (customer-reported flaky release hook). Notes: this PR intentionally keeps the scope small and does not replace the canonical CI graph; it is a developer convenience and a dev+SRE safety net that feeds signals back into the main pipeline. See review comments for small follow-ups (formatting, additional telemetry).

release_notes: - Added local developer presubmit runner (local-ci-prober) for fast, hermetic preflight checks.- Added deterministic dependency provenance stamp to attach to build artifacts for better postmortem and rollback support.- New optional presubmit-fastpath GitHub workflow for fast feedback on infra-only changes.
notes_for_backport: No backport required; dev tooling only. If backporting to release branches, ensure ci.fast_preflight.enabled is disabled by default.
how_to_verify: 1) checkout branch and run 'make preflight-local' 2) run 'tools/local-ci-prober --offline --manifest=examples/local-preflight-example.yaml' and confirm exit code 0 on a healthy tree 3) run 'go run scripts/provenance-stamp.go --manifest examples/local-preflight-example.yaml' and confirm provenance.json is reproducible across two runs on the same machine 4) inspect .github/workflows/presubmit-fastpath.yaml in CI run logs to confirm prober step executed
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: people may rely on the prober as a substitute for full CI and miss integration-level failures. Mitigation: the prober is opt-in and documented as lightweight; release automation still runs the full canonical graph and will block merges when critical checks fail. We added prominent CONTRIBUTING notes and an internal blog post to set expectations.
authors_notes: Small follow-ups planned: 1) add lightweight per-plugin telemetry if teams opt-in 2) add support for language-specific local shims contributed by SDK teams 3) optional quick-fuzz stage for release hooks in a future PR
